reasons: The gap is correctly identified: p0025 only makes Customer liable for the Content and IP therein, and the cited warranty/trademark provisions do not allocate ownership of deliverables, work product or Customer-supplied data, so no proprietary-rights article exists.

The inserted subsection reaches the playbook's preferred position with a single, self-contained addition: Customer retains all right, title and interest in Content, Properties, Requests and other Customer Data; Kubient retains the Auction Platform and pre-existing IP (consistent with its own ownership warranty, so no internal conflict); Kubient assigns deliverables/work product created for Customer; a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence back covers embedded Kubient IP; and joint ownership and any assignment of Customer IP/data to Kubient are expressly excluded.

No existing operative text was altered, so the high changed-character footprint is attributable solely to the necessary new clause, and the deterministic checks confirm no residual assignment of Customer IP/data to the vendor.

The narrow vendor-side use right ('solely as necessary to provide the Services') is a proportionate, protective addition rather than scope creep, and keeps the clause workable given Kubient must process Requests and visitor data (p0011, p0035).
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, correctly cites the playbook position, and does not overstate the deviation.
Minor drafting caveat for the drafter (not disqualifying): confirm the host section does not already contain a subsection (b) so the new lettering does not collide; renumber if it does.
